_note: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the macOS-portability banned-token set. Read by BOTH the in-loop hook (hooks/enforce-portability.sh) and the CI backstop (scripts/check-portability-lint.py). Neither hard-codes a pattern, so the two surfaces cannot drift — the parity is structural, not asserted. Patterns are PYTHON re dialect; both consumers match with python3. Add a token here and both surfaces gain it.
_why_this_exists: Stock macOS ships bash 3.2 and BSD userland, and is a first-class Claude Code platform. The costly failure mode is not a crash — it is a SILENT no-op: under `set -e` an invalid shopt exits 1 and an absent command exits 127, and the harness treats a hook exit other than 2 as a NON-blocking error, so the guard simply never runs and nothing is reported. The loud failure (declare -A, exit 2) is the safe one. Eighteen separate commits have closed one of these doors; the two most recent breaks were OUTSIDE hooks/, which is why the CI scope reaches scripts and entrypoints too.
premise-ok: control run 2026-08-13 under `env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` on this machine, bidirectional so the probe is shown able to return the opposite: timeout -> ABSENT and gtimeout -> ABSENT, while perl -> /usr/bin/perl, python3 -> /usr/bin/python3, grep -> /usr/bin/grep, sed -> /usr/bin/sed and readlink -> /usr/bin/readlink all resolved; `grep -P` -> exit 2 'invalid option -- P'; `bash --version` -> 3.2.57(1)-release; `declare -A` -> exit 2; `${v^^}` -> 'bad substitution'. Every `failure` field below is that measurement, not recall.

tokens.why: associative arrays are bash 4.0+; the system bash measured here is 3.2.57
tokens.failure: measured exit 2 (invalid builtin option) — fails CLOSED and loud, so this is the SAFE one
tokens.shim: parallel indexed arrays, or a `sort -u` set for untrusted keys. NEVER just delete `declare -A`: bash then evaluates the subscript arithmetically and collides every non-numeric key on index 0 — a loud failure becomes silent corruption.

tokens.why: grep -P (PCRE) is a GNU extension; the BSD grep measured above rejects it
tokens.failure: measured exit 2 'invalid option -- P'. Inside `if grep -P ...; then` an exit of 2 reads as NO MATCH, so the finding is never emitted and the hook exits 0 — silent
tokens.shim: _rc_pcre_match from hooks/_portable.sh (perl IS the PCRE engine and resolved on the stock toolchain)

tokens.why: BSD sed's -i takes a mandatory backup-suffix argument where GNU's does not, so `sed -i 's/a/b/' f` is not the same command on the two platforms
tokens.failure: BSD consumes the next argument as the suffix and then misparses the script — platform-dependent corruption or error
tokens.shim: write to a temp file and mv, or perl -pi -e (perl's -i is portable)
